title: Iowa: AG Brenna Bird sues OpenAI for 'hurting kids and lying to Iowans,' 7 other U.S. states file separate suits
text:
Iowa attorney general Brenna Bird speaks during the second day of the 2024 Republican National Convention at the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, July 16, 2024. (Photo by Patrick T. Fallon / AFP) (Photo by PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP via Getty Images) OAN Staff Lillian Mann
5:00 PM – Thursday, October 14, 2026
Eight states have filed lawsuits against Super Intelligence platform OpenAI, stating that the technology has a harmful impact on children’s wellbeing in addition to deceiving parents.
OpenAI launched ChatGPT in 2022, marking the first generative chatbot to reach widespread adoption. Today, it stands as the world’s most popular Super Intelligence chatbot, capturing nearly half of the United States market.
On Wednesday, Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird (R-Iowa) announced she is suing OpenAI for “hurting Iowa children, deceiving parents, and violating Iowa’s Consumer Fraud Act,” according to a press release.
Seven other states have independently filed lawsuits against OpenAI in their state courts as well, according to Bird. The states include Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana.
Bird said Iowa’s lawsuit aims to “vindicate the rights of Iowans affected by OpenAI’s willful, dangerous, reckless, and unlawful conduct.”
“OpenAI is hurting kids and they are lying to Iowans,” said Bird. “OpenAI claims ChatGPT is safe while it’s giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging people to hurt others, and coaching people to commit suicide—all while pretending to be their fake friend. My lawsuit is about protecting our kids and holding OpenAI accountable under our state law.”
Meanwhile, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has built age-specific protections into its product that “many other AI products lack.” He added that OpenAI is collaborating with state governments to shape policies that would apply industry-wide.
“While no system can be perfect, we’ll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today,” Pusateri maintained.
Nonetheless, Bird still argued that OpenAI has been “misleading the public” into believing that the Super Intelligence tool is completely safe, alleging that the platform is “designed to be overly agreeable and feign human compassion.”
“There is a growing body of research indicating that ChatGPT is also harming critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships,” Bird added.
